name: EM-9017

lead: EM-9017 is a steroid-based selective androgen receptor modulator that appears in patents from Endorech, the group associated with Fernand Labrie. The idea behind compounds of its class is to act on the androgen receptor differently in different tissues.
Its appeal for physique is the muscle-supporting side of that profile. It has only been described in animal models in patent documents and has not been tested in people.

paras: It binds the androgen receptor. Patent descriptions say compounds in the series inhibit prostate and seminal vesicle tissue in rats while stimulating a perineal muscle, the pattern that defines a SARM.

No human safety data exist. It is not approved or marketed, so it has no regulatory label. Steroidal androgen-receptor ligands as a class can affect hormone balance, but the specific effects of EM-9017 in people are unknown.

angle.text: EM-9017 is described in patent filings as a steroidal SARM whose muscle-stimulating activity in rats coexists with prostate inhibition. People interested in lean mass look at SARMs for this tissue-selective profile, though the compound has only been described preclinically.

lead: EM-9017 is an experimental steroidal selective androgen receptor modulator (SARM) that appears in patent filings from the Quebec-based Endorecherche/Endorech group, whose work was led by Fernand Labrie. It belongs to a family of steroids carrying a substituent at the 17-alpha position, designed to block androgen receptors in some tissues such as the prostate while acting as a mild agonist, or neutral, in others such as muscle [1].

For someone interested in appearance, the interest in this kind of molecule is the muscle side of the profile: a SARM that supports muscle tissue while dampening androgen action in the prostate is the profile that physique-minded readers look for in compounds of this class. Patent literature describes compounds of the series in animal models, where muscle stimulation was observed alongside prostate and seminal vesicle inhibition [1].
EM-9017 has not been approved anywhere and no human trials have been published. Information is limited to patent documents and preclinical descriptions.

paras: EM-9017 is a steroid-based molecule with a modified 17-alpha side chain. The patent family it belongs to covers 17-alpha-substituted steroids intended as systemic antiandrogens and as SARMs [1]. Unlike non-steroidal SARMs such as ostarine, which are built around aryl-amide scaffolds, compounds in this series keep the four-ring steroid core.

Patent text describes SARMs of the series as having antagonist activity in tissues such as the prostate while showing little activity or agonist activity elsewhere [1]. Related Endorecherche compounds, such as EM-5854, have their own Wikipedia entries, which places EM-9017 within a numbered laboratory series.

Wikipedia describes selective androgen receptor modulators as drugs that activate the androgen receptor in certain tissues, aiming for muscle and bone effects with less impact on the prostate; the concept grew out of nonsteroidal antiandrogens developed in the 1970s, the first nonsteroidal SARMs appeared in 1998 and the term was introduced in 1999.[2] It notes that steroidal SARMs also exist, giving YK-11 and MK-0773 as examples, which is the structural group EM-9017 belongs to.[2]

According to the same article, no SARM has been approved by the FDA or EMA, some have increased lean mass in trials without clear functional gains, the World Anti-Doping Agency banned SARMs in 2008, and recreational use has been linked to case reports of drug-induced liver injury.[2]

EM-9017 is listed among experimental androgen-receptor ligands as a steroidal SARM. It has little presence in community discussion, and no consumer product or established community protocol for it is documented. Gray-market SARMs in general are sold as research chemicals, and Wikipedia reports one study found most online products were mislabeled.[2]

No studies found. Animal data are limited to descriptions in patent filings, in which compounds of the series were reported to reduce prostate and seminal vesicle weight in rats while stimulating the bulbocavernosus muscle [1].
EM-9017 is not approved as a medicine in any jurisdiction and is not marketed.
